rounds.text: The market capitalization of ₹ 675 Cr sits alongside a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.81x on a book value of ₹ 42.9 per share [E2, E3]. Capital work-in-progress (CWIP) stands at ₹ 11 Cr for March 2026, representing a massive 266.7% increase year-on-year that signals an active capex build-up phase and future growth spend [E27]. This expansionary posture aligns directly with the scanX signal engine, which identifies accelerating earnings growth as a core bull reason [E43]. Furthermore, the broader sector enjoys a robust median profit growth of 17.9% and positive median sales growth of 7.8%, providing a supportive operating tailwind [E52, E53]. Conceded: trailing twelve-month profit growth is down by -83% and sales have contracted by -21% [E14, E15].

The valuation is fundamentally detached from the operational reality of the business, highlighted by a staggering trailing P/E ratio of 278x [E1]. This extreme multiple is completely unsupported by the core financial performance, as evidenced by a severe contraction in top-line and bottom-line metrics, including a 21 percent drop in compounded sales growth and an 83 percent collapse in compounded profit growth over the trailing twelve months [E14, E15]. Operational efficiency is severely lagging behind industry standards, with a negative return on assets of -2.89% contrasting sharply against the sector benchmark of 3.07% [E8]. Furthermore, the enterprise value relative to earnings is massively bloated, with an EV/EBITDA of 87.93x compared to a sector benchmark of just 9.02x [E11]. The stock also triggers direct warnings about a rich valuation blind-spot, confirming that the current price already heavily discounts any potential good news [E50]. Conceded: the price-to-book ratio sits at a relatively modest 1.81x on a book value of 42.9 [E2], and capital work-in-progress is expanding with a 266.7% move up to Rs 11 Cr [E27].

Conceded: trailing sales and profit growth show a contraction of -21% and -83% respectively [E14, E15]. However, the scanX signal engine explicitly flags that earnings growth is accelerating, proving that backward-looking figures miss the inflection point [E43]. While the trailing P/E of 278x looks extreme [E1], the price-to-book ratio sits at a modest 1.81x on a book value of 42.9 [E2], indicating asset backing that the multiple distorts. The significant 266.7% surge in capital work-in-progress to Rs 11 Cr directly demonstrates that an active capex build-up and growth spend are underway [E27]. Conceded: return on assets and EV/EBITDA lag sector benchmarks [E8, E11], yet these trailing metrics fail to account for the ongoing capital deployment that rides on a sector median profit growth tailwind of 17.9% [E52].

Conceded: the company shows a 266.7% surge in capital work-in-progress to Rs 11 Cr [E27]. However, the bull's reliance on the scanX signal engine regarding accelerating earnings [E43] is completely undermined by actual filed statements confirming a catastrophic 83% collapse in compounded profit growth and a 21% contraction in sales [E14, E15]. While the bull points to a modest price-to-book ratio of 1.81x [E2], this ignores the company's deeply negative return on assets of -2.89% and an extreme EV/EBITDA of 87.93x against a sector benchmark of just 9.02x [E8, E11]. Furthermore, attempting to dismiss a trailing P/E of 278x [E1] as a distortion fails a basic valuation bias check, which warns that such rich pricing already dangerously discounts any potential future recovery [E50]. Finally, pointing to a sector median profit growth tailwind of 17.9% [E52] offers zero protection when the firm's own metrics are aggressively moving in the exact opposite direction.
